title: CT Exemption Application Deadlines
hook: Exempt from Corporate Tax? You still have to apply.
caption:
Exempt from Corporate Tax? You still have to apply.

FTA Decision No. 15 of 2026 replaced Decision No. 7 of 2023 from 15 September 2026.

The new timelines:

1. Register for Corporate Tax first, then apply for exemption.

2. General rule: apply within 90 Business Days after the end of the Tax Period.

3. Persons covered by Cabinet Decision No. 55 of 2025: apply by 31 December 2026.

4. Certain wholly owned subsidiaries, for Tax Periods ended before 1 January 2026: apply by 31 October 2026.

5. An approved exemption applies from the start of the Tax Period in the application.

Subsidiaries apply only after their parent has applied.

✅ 31 October is less than three weeks away. Check now if it applies to you.

✅ Get the parent's application in first.

Is your group's exemption application ready?

General information, not tax advice.

title: VAT Employee Expenses Input Tax
hook: 6 employee benefits where you can now recover VAT.
caption:
6 employee benefits where you can now recover VAT.

FTA Decision No. 17 of 2026 took effect on 1 October.

It covers goods and services you give employees free of charge.

You need a contract or documented policy, and every condition for that case must be met.

1. Transport: home-to-work, client sites or job duties, with no cash-allowance option.

2. Food and drinks: only where staff are at remote sites with no food facilities or restaurants nearby.

3. Accommodation: operationally required, near the work site, with no cash alternative.

4. New joiners' housing: temporary, up to 30 days.

5. Phones, data and home internet: needed for work, with a documented usage policy and reasonable monitoring.

6. Parking: business use only, a documented policy, and receipts showing date, time, amount and tax.

✅ Check your employment contracts first. A cash-allowance option can block recovery on transport and accommodation.

✅ Then line up your policies and receipts before your next VAT return.

Which of these benefits does your business provide today?

title: VAT Decree Law Amendments VATP046
hook: 5 VAT law changes every UAE business should know.
caption:
5 VAT law changes every UAE business should know.

The FTA's Public Clarification VATP046 explains recent amendments to the VAT Decree-Law.

Here is what matters for your books:

1. Excess recoverable VAT must now be used or refunded within 5 years from the end of the Tax Period it arose in. This applies from 1 January 2026.

2. Reverse-charge imports: you no longer issue a tax invoice to yourself, but you still account for the VAT.

3. Input tax can be rejected if your supply chain is linked to tax evasion and you knew, or should have known.

4. E-invoicing is now part of the VAT law. Obligations apply as the phased rollout reaches your business.

5. E-invoices issued through the system must be kept electronically.

✅ Review old VAT credit balances against the 5-year limit.

✅ Document your supplier checks. "I didn't know" is no longer enough.

Which of these changes affects your business most?

General information, not tax advice.

title: VAT Digital Currency Conversion
hook: Paid in crypto? Here's how the FTA wants it valued.
caption:
Paid in crypto? Here's how the FTA wants it valued.

Directive on Tax Transactions No. 3 of 2026 sets one method for VAT.

It covers supplies of digital currency and supplies paid for in digital currency.

The method:

1. Choose 3 platforms from the FTA's list.

2. Use the same 3 for the whole calendar year.

3. Take each platform's rate at the date and time of supply or payment, as applicable.

4. Convert to AED using the average of the 3 rates.

5. Keep a record of each rate.

The platforms named: Binance FZE, Bybit Fintech FZE, Deribit FZE, Bitget and Payward FZCO.

Directives bind both the FTA and taxpayers.

✅ Pick your 3 platforms now and build the calculation into your VAT process.

✅ Save rate evidence with every invoice.

Does your business accept digital currency yet?

General information, not tax advice.

title: VAT Judicial Expert Services
hook: Court-appointed experts: your fees are subject to VAT.
caption:
Court-appointed experts: your fees are subject to VAT.

Directive on Tax Transactions No. 1 of 2026 settles the question.

Services by a Judicial Expert appointed by a competent court:

1. Are supplied in the course of Business in the UAE.

2. Are Taxable Supplies under the VAT Law.

3. Any amount received is Consideration for a supply of services.

4. The expert must register for VAT where the registration requirements are met.

5. It makes no difference if a Government Entity pays.

A Judicial Expert is a person on the roster of experts with the Ministry of Justice, a local judicial authority or an arbitration centre.

✅ If you act as a court-appointed expert, check whether your income crosses the registration threshold.

✅ Account for VAT on these engagements from now on.

Do you know an expert witness who needs to see this?

General information, not tax advice.

title: VAT Life Insurance Fees
hook: Life insurance is VAT-exempt. Are the fees around it?
caption:
Life insurance is VAT-exempt. Are the fees around it?

Directive on Tax Transactions No. 4 of 2026 answers when fees connected to a life insurance or reinsurance contract share its exemption.

The conditions:

1. The service must be necessary for, and directly connected to, providing or transferring the contract.

2. The fee must be included in the premium, with no separate charge.

3. This can cover fees for managing, operating or executing the contract.

4. Independent or separately charged services are separate supplies for VAT.

5. The final answer depends on the facts of each case.

✅ Insurers: review how your fees are structured and billed.

✅ A separately invoiced fee can change the VAT outcome.

How are fees shown on your policy documents today?

General information, not tax advice.

title: E Invoicing Service Provider Accreditation
hook: Choosing an e-invoicing provider? Check these rules first.
caption:
Choosing an e-invoicing provider? Check these rules first.

Ministerial Decision No. 64 of 2025, amended by Ministerial Decision No. 56 of 2026, sets who can be accredited.

What a provider must show:

1. New: its e-invoicing product must have operated for at least 2 years.

2. Active Peppol certification, with OpenPeppol conformance tests passed.

3. Paid-up capital of AED 50,000, plus ISO 22301 and ISO/IEC 27001.

4. Insurance: professional indemnity AED 2.5m, crime AED 5m, cyber fraud AED 5m.

5. Accreditation lasts 2 years, with renewal at least 70 Business Days before expiry.

✅ Only work with providers accredited by the Ministry of Finance.

✅ Check how your ERP will connect to your provider before you sign.

Have you picked your e-invoicing provider yet?

title: CT Director and Officer Connected Persons
hook: Director or officer? It's about authority, not job title.
caption:
Director or officer? It's about authority, not job title.

Under Article 36 of the Corporate Tax Law, payments to directors and officers are deductible only at Market Value.

Public Clarification CTP010 explains who counts:

1. Director: a member of the board, or equivalent body, under the constitutional documents.

2. A "director" job title alone doesn't make someone a director.

3. Officer: someone with authority to plan, direct and control, make strategic decisions, or bind the company.

4. Conduct counts. Exercising that authority makes you an officer, whatever your title.

5. Only a natural person can be a director or officer.

✅ List everyone with real decision-making power, not only the board.

✅ Test their pay and benefits against Market Value before you file.

Who in your company would count as an officer?

General information, not tax advice.

title: CT AT1 Instruments Banks
hook: Banks: AT1 coupons outside P&L are not deductible.
caption:
Banks: AT1 coupons outside P&L are not deductible.

That is the FTA's position in Public Clarification CTP012.

The reasoning:

1. Taxable Income starts from Accounting Income, the net profit or loss in the financial statements (Article 20).

2. Payments on Additional Tier 1 instruments that are not included in Accounting Income are not deductible.

3. "Payments" means coupons or dividends, not repayment of principal.

4. AT1 instruments classed as equity under IFRS typically pay coupons through equity, not profit or loss.

5. How AT1 holders are taxed is outside this clarification.

The outcome follows the accounting treatment.

✅ Banks: confirm how each AT1 instrument is classified before your next return.

✅ Model the tax impact of equity versus liability treatment.

Does this change how you would structure future AT1 issues?

General information, not tax advice.

title: Free Zones vs Designated Zones TAXP010
hook: "We're in a Free Zone, so we're covered." Not necessarily.
caption:
"We're in a Free Zone, so we're covered." Not necessarily.

Public Clarification TAXP010 shows Corporate Tax, VAT and Excise Tax each define their zones differently.

Key points:

1. A VAT Designated Zone isn't automatically a Designated Zone for Corporate Tax.

2. A Corporate Tax Designated Zone must be both a VAT Designated Zone and a Corporate Tax Free Zone.

3. The 0% rate on qualifying distribution income applies only in or from a Corporate Tax Designated Zone.

4. An Excise Designated Zone needs security controls, customs supervision and a Warehouse Keeper.

5. A Qualifying Free Zone Person that breaches the conditions loses its status for that period and the next four.

✅ Check your zone's status separately for each tax.

✅ Remember: 0% applies only to Qualifying Income.

Has your team checked your zone status for each tax?

General information, not tax advice.

title: Pillar Two Top up Tax Registration Deadlines
caption:
Top-up Tax: register by 30 November 2026.

FTA Decision No. 12 of 2026 sets the timelines for UAE entities of multinational groups.

The deadlines:

1. Register within 7 months of the end of the first in-scope Fiscal Year.

2. Fiscal Year ended before 30 April 2026? Register by 30 November 2026.

3. Deregister within 6 months of ceasing to exist or leaving the group.

4. Entity ceased before 30 June 2026? Deregister by 31 December 2026.

5. Group fell out of scope? Notify within 6 months. Back in scope? Notify within 7 months.

You can't deregister until all Top-up Tax and penalties are paid and all returns are filed.

✅ Put 30 November in the diary now.

✅ Decide whether one entity will file for the whole group.

Is your group's registration plan in place?

General information, not tax advice.

title: Pillar Two Scope and Registration Guide
hook: Is your group in scope of UAE Top-up Tax?
caption:
Is your group in scope of UAE Top-up Tax?

The FTA's guide TTGREG1 explains who must register for the Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax.

Key points:

1. In scope: multinational groups with revenue of EUR 750 million or more in at least 2 of the 4 preceding Fiscal Years.

2. It applies to Fiscal Years beginning on or after 1 January 2025.

3. Purely domestic UAE groups are out of scope, whatever their revenue.

4. You must register even if your Top-up Tax is zero, for example under a safe harbour.

5. Late registration costs AED 10,000 per Entity.

Top-up Tax registration is separate from Corporate Tax registration.

✅ Run the revenue test for the last 4 years now.

✅ Fiscal Year ended before 30 April 2026? Your deadline is 30 November 2026.

Has your group confirmed whether it is in scope?

General information, not tax advice.

#UAECorporateTax #CFO #SMEsUAE

title: Pillar Two Excluded Entities Guide
hook: Exempt from Corporate Tax doesn't mean exempt from Top-up Tax.
caption:
Exempt from Corporate Tax doesn't mean exempt from Top-up Tax.

The FTA's guide TTGEIE1 explains which entities sit outside the Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax.

Key points:

1. Excluded Entities include international organisations, non-profits, pension funds, and investment funds or REIVs that are the Ultimate Parent Entity.

2. Subsidiaries can qualify at 95%+ ownership with holding activities, or 85%+ with substantially all income excluded.

3. Ownership is measured by value, not share count.

4. Corporate Tax exemption and Excluded Entity status are separate tests.

5. Excluded entities don't register or file, but their revenue still counts towards the EUR 750m threshold.

✅ Test each UAE entity against Pillar Two separately from its Corporate Tax status.

✅ Check ownership by value, not shares.

Has your group mapped each entity under both regimes?

General information, not tax advice.

title: Excise Tobacco and E Liquid Minimum Price
hook: New excise floors for tobacco and vapes from 1 September.
caption:
New excise floors for tobacco and vapes from 1 September.

Cabinet Decision No. 137 of 2026 sets minimum Excise Prices, the value excise tax is calculated on.

The floors:

1. Cigarettes, normal or electrically heated: at least AED 0.40 per cigarette.

2. Water pipe tobacco and similar products: at least AED 0.10 per gram.

3. E-cigarette liquids: at least AED 1 per ml, with or without nicotine.

4. These are minimum tax bases, not tax rates or retail prices.

5. The Decision replaces Cabinet Decision No. 55 of 2019.

The Excise Price is still calculated as before, but it can't fall below these floors.

✅ Producers and importers: check every product against the new floors.

✅ Include nicotine-free e-liquids in your review.

Has your pricing been checked against the new floors?

General information, not tax advice.

title: Tax Procedures Executive Regulation Amendments
hook: Found an error in a past return? 20 Business Days.
caption:
Found an error in a past return? 20 Business Days.

Cabinet Decision No. 17 of 2026 amended the Executive Regulation of the Tax Procedures Law from 1 April 2026.

What it means:

1. Error above AED 10,000: file a Voluntary Disclosure within 20 Business Days of becoming aware.

2. Error of AED 10,000 or less: correct it in your next return.

3. Overstated refund claims need a Voluntary Disclosure within 20 Business Days.

4. Refund decisions are made within 20 Business Days, unless the FTA notifies you of a longer period.

5. Refund still pending? Keep your records for an extra 2 years.

These rules apply across VAT, Excise and Corporate Tax.

✅ Set an internal process so errors reach your tax team fast.

✅ Extend record retention while refunds are pending.

How quickly does an error reach your tax team today?

General information, not tax advice.

title: Private Clarifications Guide
hook: Unsure how a tax rule applies to you? Ask the FTA.
caption:
Unsure how a tax rule applies to you? Ask the FTA.

The FTA's updated Private Clarifications guide (TPGPC1) now covers VAT, Excise, Corporate Tax and Top-up Tax.

Key points:

1. Fee: AED 1,500 for one tax, AED 2,250 for more than one.

2. The FTA responds within 60 Business Days, longer for complex cases.

3. If the FTA asks for more information, you have 40 Business Days to reply.

4. Withdraw within 2 Business Days of submitting to get the fee back.

5. Only registered Tax Agents or Legal Representatives can apply for someone else.

A Private Clarification binds the FTA only for you, and only on the facts you gave.

✅ Check existing FTA guides and public clarifications first.

✅ Give complete facts. The answer is only as good as the request.

Have you ever applied for a Private Clarification?

General information, not tax advice.

title: FTA Clarifications Policy and APAs
hook: Want certainty on transfer pricing? Look at the unilateral APA route.
caption:
Want certainty on transfer pricing? Look at the unilateral APA route.

The FTA's updated policy on clarifications took effect on 1 March 2026.

On Unilateral Advance Pricing Agreements:

1. They currently cover domestic Related Party transactions. Cross-border applications are expected from Q4 2026.

2. Threshold: expected transactions of at least AED 100 million per Tax Period.

3. Each agreement covers 3 to 5 Tax Periods.

4. The FTA aims to conclude within 30 months of a complete application.

5. Administrative exceptions are valid for 3 years.

Because you apply well before the first covered period, early planning matters.

✅ Groups with large domestic related-party flows: map them against the AED 100m threshold.

✅ Start pre-filing talks early.

Would an APA give your group more certainty?

General information, not tax advice.

title: Seized and Abandoned Goods Disposal
hook: Goods seized? The FTA can auction them early.
caption:
Goods seized? The FTA can auction them early.

FTA Decision No. 7 of 2026 took effect on 30 July 2026.

It sets the procedure for selling seized and abandoned goods by public auction.

Key points:

1. It covers goods that are perishable, at risk of shortage or leakage, or hazardous.

2. Goods under investigation or in court proceedings need prior approval from the prosecution or court.

3. The owner is notified before the sale.

4. Proceeds pay costs first, then tax, then penalties. Any surplus goes to the owner.

5. Waiting can cost you the goods, not just the tax.

✅ If your goods are seized, settle what's due quickly.

✅ Ask for the goods back in writing before an auction date is set.

Has your business had goods held by the FTA before?

General information, not tax advice.
